result.topic_en: On polar integral equations: instead of convergence of the sum of squared Fourier coefficients, the series $\sum c_n^2/|\lambda_n|$ converges for a definite kernel, followed by the simplest example $u''+\lambda V(x)u=0$ with $V(x)$ the sign of $x$ on $[-1,1]$.

items.english: For the polar eigenfunctions arising from a polar integral equation, we cannot conclude that the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients converges for an arbitrary continuous function, but instead that c_1^2/|λ_1| + c_2^2/|λ_2| + ... always converges.
